name: Manasseh
overview: Manasseh is a male biblical figure noted primarily as the father of Gershom, as recorded in Judges 18:30. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided for him in the biblical text. His identity is defined chiefly by his paternal role.
namesAndTitles: The name Manasseh means 'one that makes to forget,' reflecting a Hebrew origin. This proper name was not given directly by God, according to Judges 18:30, but it carries a meaningful designation within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Manasseh as the father of Gershom, as noted in Judges 18:30. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical record for this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Manasseh's significance in Scripture is tied to his role as the father of Gershom, linking him to the broader narrative of the tribes of Israel. Although he is not described with tribal affiliation here, prior biblical references identify Manasseh as Joseph's firstborn son, whose descendants became a prominent tribe. The distinction in blessing between Manasseh and his brother Ephraim underscores God's sovereign choice beyond human customs, highlighting the divine orchestration in Israel's history.
